note: Source of truth for architecture decisions. tools/gen-architecture.mjs renders this into DECISIONS.md and the ADR table in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md. status is 'decided' or 'assumption' (an assumption was made without the owner's input and should be confirmed).

decisions.title: Ingestion is a Cloud Run job, not a service
decisions.decision: The ingester runs to completion and exits; it listens on no port.
decisions.why: Pulling a museum's API is a batch with a beginning and an end. A job is billed only while it works and cannot be reached from the internet at all.

decisions.title: The planner is stateless
decisions.decision: A plan is a pure function of the request and the stored museum. Replanning is another POST /api/plan carrying the current gallery, the objects already seen, and the wings to skip; the browser holds that state.
decisions.why: No sessions means no session store, instances can scale to zero between visits, and any instance can answer any request.

decisions.title: The planner serves the web frontend
decisions.decision: Static files ship inside the planner image and are served from /.
decisions.why: One deployable and one URL for the demo. Same origin, so no CORS. A separate frontend service would add a deploy step and nothing else.

decisions.title: Firestore is the only shared state, behind a schema contract
decisions.decision: ingestion-job is the sole writer and planner has read-only IAM. The document shapes are contracts in contracts/firestore, and each side validates them with its own models.
decisions.why: The brief fixes the system at five pieces, so there is no data-API service between the two deployables. Treating the documents as a versioned contract with one writer gives the same decoupling without a sixth piece.

decisions.title: Pub/Sub is pulled by the job; Cloud Scheduler starts the job
decisions.decision: Publishing {museum_id} to topic ingest-museum queues a museum. The job drains the pull subscription at the start of every execution. A Scheduler tick starts an execution every 10 minutes; deploy/add-museum.sh publishes and starts one immediately.
decisions.why: Pub/Sub push cannot start a Cloud Run job directly, and the usual bridge (Eventarc plus Workflows) would add two pieces. Pull-and-drain keeps the job a job and keeps adding a museum to one publish, at the cost of up to 10 minutes of delay.

decisions.title: Objects are stored in chunk documents
decisions.decision: Up to 250 normalized objects per Firestore document under museums/{id}/object_chunks.
decisions.why: A planner cold start loads a whole museum. One document per object would cost about 1,500 reads per cold start and leave the free tier on launch day; chunks cost about 6.

decisions.title: The museum document is written last
decisions.decision: An ingest run writes the floor graph, then the chunks, then deletes stale chunks, then the museum document, whose chunk_count is the pointer readers trust.
decisions.why: A run that fails halfway never leaves readers pointing at half-written data, without needing a transaction across hundreds of kilobytes.

decisions.title: Objects without a gallery are dropped at ingestion
decisions.decision: The object schema requires a non-empty gallery, so an object the museum's API does not place in a gallery never reaches Firestore.
decisions.why: Never invent gallery numbers. Enforcing it at the data boundary means the planner cannot plan such an object even by mistake.

decisions.title: The floor graph is hand-built, coarse, and says how far it has been verified
decisions.decision: One JSON graph per museum, bundled in the ingestion image. A node is a run of adjacent galleries on one level. The graph carries a verification status that every plan repeats in its notices.
decisions.why: No collection API describes which galleries connect or where the elevators are. A coarse graph can be built by hand in a day; saying plainly that it is unverified is the honest way to ship it.

decisions.title: Unknown means not step-free
decisions.decision: An edge is step_free only when the published plan supports it. A connection we are unsure about is marked not step-free and given a name.
decisions.why: Wrongly saying no step-free route exists costs a visitor a suggestion. Wrongly saying one exists can strand them at a staircase.

decisions.title: plan.step_free is computed, never echoed
decisions.decision: The planner derives step_free from the segments the plan actually uses and asserts invariants I1 and I2 before responding; on failure it returns an error rather than a plan.
decisions.why: The claim a wheelchair user relies on must not depend on the request flag being threaded through correctly.

decisions.title: Greedy scoring and routing
decisions.decision: Score objects by interest and tag overlap weighted by the constraint profile, then repeatedly take the best feasible stop from the current position using shortest paths on the graph.
decisions.why: Good enough beats optimal for a visit of a dozen stops, it is easy to explain, and it is deterministic, so replanning never surprises.

decisions.title: Why-sentences come from templates, not a language model
decisions.decision: Each sentence is assembled from the object's own tags and fields, and the response lists which fields were used.
decisions.why: Every claim must be grounded in the museum's data. Templates cannot hallucinate, cost nothing, and add no dependency.

decisions.title: Services share contracts, not code
decisions.decision: Each deployable has its own models and tests them against /contracts. Nothing is imported across services.
decisions.why: Either side can be rewritten or redeployed alone, and `gcloud run deploy --source` uploads one directory at a time anyway.

decisions.title: A file-backed store for offline tests
decisions.decision: Both deployables accept STORE_BACKEND=file, which reads and writes the same documents as JSON files in the Firestore layout.
decisions.why: The whole pipeline (ingest a fixture, then plan from it) can be tested with nothing but Python: no emulator, no Java, no Docker, no GCP.

decisions.title: Contract tooling has zero dependencies
decisions.decision: tools/*.mjs validates the contracts, the floor graphs, and planner responses using only Node's standard library, including a small parser for the YAML subset the OpenAPI file uses. CI also runs openapi-spec-validator as an independent check.
decisions.why: The gate has to run on a machine where nothing can be installed. It tests itself (tools/selftest.mjs) so a green result means something.

decisions.title: The planner is public and stores nothing about visitors
decisions.decision: Unauthenticated ingress, no accounts, no cookies, no request bodies logged, no secrets.
decisions.why: What a visitor's body can do is sensitive. The simplest way to protect it is never to keep it.

decisions.title: Hard caps on scale
decisions.decision: Planner: 0 to 3 instances, concurrency 40. Job: one task, one retry, 30-minute timeout, 1,500 objects per museum.
decisions.why: A launch-day spike can slow the app down but cannot produce a surprising bill.

decisions.title: Art Institute of Chicago is the second museum
decisions.decision: The second adapter targets the AIC API.
decisions.why: Its records carry a gallery title for works on view, which is the one field planning needs. Adding it shows the pipeline is not hardcoded to the Met.

decisions.title: Python 3.12 and FastAPI, as specified
decisions.decision: No change of stack was proposed.
decisions.why: The brief's stack fits: the work is I/O and data shaping, the Google client libraries are first-class, and Pydantic gives runtime validation of every contract.

decisions.title: A museum whose API cuts each run short is collected a batch at a time
decisions.decision: For such a museum the job reads back what it has stored, asks the API only for objects it lacks, and writes the merged set. The museum document says whether collection is complete, and the Scheduler tick keeps going until it is.
decisions.why: The Met's API refuses a client after about 40 object requests, at any speed we tried. Asking for a little every 10 minutes is slower but gentler on their service than retrying, and it turns the timer from a formality into the thing that fills the museum.

decisions.title: Local-first, deploy later
decisions.decision: Everything is built and tested offline; deployment is a parameterized script and workflow that run once a GCP project and GitHub repository exist.
decisions.why: No cloud credentials were available during the build. Nothing in the repo claims to be deployed until a real request has been made against it.
